title: Surge priming playbook and release checklist (personal scratch)
content:
Context:
Quick personal notebook for release windows where we expect client traffic surges (campaigns, partner events). Focus is on safe priming so that cold caches, kv-warmup, and batching thresholds don't spike latency/cost or trigger noisy rollbacks. This is a working checklist — lots of TODOs and heuristics below.

High-level approach (goal):
- Keep tail latency < 300ms for 95th under normal surge.
- Limit cost delta to < 1.5x baseline for first 30 minutes.
- If failure or bad quality, escape hatch should drop to fallback model or 0 traffic in < 90s.

Preflight (T-48h to T-1h):
- Sanity: confirm model version pinned in routing config and SDK flag (release-pin: v2025-02-10-rc3).
- Canary plan: reserve 1% client cohort + two warmup cohorts (0.5% each) for progressive priming.
- Capacity: verify dedicated pool size, pre-warm 2 GPUs for hot path.
- Alerts: create temporary alert rules for latency, OOMs, KF cache miss rate, and hallucination rate (eval-run metric).
- Smoke tests: run synthetic long-context generation + embeddings carnival (see linked PR).
- Stakeholders: message #releases + rotation list (oncall + product) with timeline.

Priming sequence (T0 = start of release):
1) Canary open: route 0.1% -> canary variant for 5m. Verify successful responses and no error increase.
2) Cohort A warmup: route 0.5% -> priming path for 10m. Send batched synthetic bursts mimicking client distribution (tool: /scripts/priming/loadgen --profile campaign).
3) Cohort B warmup: add second 0.5% and repeat bursts with slightly higher concurrency to exercise batching.
4) Monitor: 1m granularity for 15m; check metrics below. If green, advance to 2% steady for 20m.
5) Ramp: incremental doubling every 20–30m until target fraction.

Key telemetry (signals to watch):
- invocation-latency.p95 (ms)
- error-rate.total (5m)
- kv-cache.miss-rate (5m)
- batch-size.median
- cost-per-token.delta
- hallucination-flag.rate (from eval hooks)

Hard thresholds (escape hatch):
- p95 > 3x baseline for 10m -> immediate rollback to previous model.
- error-rate > 2% for 5m -> pause ramp and investigate.
- OOM or GPU-evictions -> immediate diversion to fallback pool.

Runbook quick commands (ops):
- shift traffic to fallback variant: curl -X POST https://internal-routing/api/switch -d '{"route":"fallback-v1","fraction":1.0}' (use admin token)
- pin user cohort back to old model: ./tools/pin-client --cohort COHORT_ID --model v2025-01-stable
- scale up pool: aws autoscale set-capacity --name redwood-dedicated-prod --desired 6

Notes-to-self / gotchas:
- Warmup bursts must mimic real interarrival times or batching will be misleading. Avoid sending constant high qps — instead, use 80/20 distribution and a few long prompts to populate KV cache.
- Avoid running global cache flushes during priming; they invalidate warming.
- If client SDKs aggressively retry on 5xx, they may magnify a small transient into overload. Consider temporary client-side backoff relaxation.
- Watch for shard imbalance: single tenant hot path may saturate one GPU; verify placement with trace.

Post-launch validation (first 2 hours):
- Check quality-sampling: run 100 prompt evals from production traffic against both canary and baseline — inspect divergence.
- Cost telemetry: compare tokens/s and billable-token rate to baseline window.
- User-visible error reports: tickets created (Slack/ops) should be < 1 per 10k users.

Postmortem template (for this run):
- Summary of what we changed (model, routing, config)
- Timeline of traffic fractions and key metrics (paste graphs)
- Decisions taken (rollforward/rollback) and who approved
- Root cause analysis (if any) and fix plan
- Action items for next priming window

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add a small prefill generator that populates per-client context templates (TODO: write generator, owner @Aisha).
- Decide whether to include a proactive token-throttle on SDK side for first 5 minutes.
- Automate cohort sequencing in the console as a reusable workflow (request: product).

Quick checklist (final preflight - short):
[ ] Model pinned in routing config
[ ] Canary cohorts created
[ ] Autoscale warmup executed
[ ] Alerts and oncall notified
[ ] Smoke tests passed
[ ] Rollback/runbook posted

Endnotes: this is a personal scratchpad; transfer finalized steps into shared playbook if this flow stabilizes. Keep a log of events in the release ticket JIRA-ENG-2543.
